lesson.menu_desc: A typhoon closes the port of Kaohsiung -- the status update, the supplier call and the leadership presentation in one crisis day
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 29 -- The Full Picture -- Integrating the B2 toolkit across a full crisis: email, call and presentation
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fabiana Michelly Silva | Lesson 29 -- The Full Picture

listenings.text: Fabiana, this is Kevin Lin from Formosa Display in Tainan. Sorry for the early call. As you may have heard, the typhoon closed the port of Kaohsiung last night, and the authorities say it will stay closed for at least four days. Our factory is fine, and nobody was hurt. The problem is your panels: twelve thousand units are sitting in the port, ready to go. I've already asked our logistics team to check flights from Taipei, but the airlines are fully booked until Monday. Honestly, we should have moved part of the order last week, when the first warnings came out. I'll send you a written update by noon your time. Please call me when you can.

Fabiana, it's Priya. Thanks for the status update this morning. It was exactly what we needed: short, clear, and honest about what we don't know yet. For the four o'clock meeting, here's what the leadership team expects. Please don't walk us through the whole story; we've all read your email. Give us three things. First, the ripple effect: which customers are hit, and when. Second, the worst-case scenario, with a real number. And third, your recommendation. If you need a decision on air freight, ask for it in the meeting, not after. Oh, and the CFO has asked that every cost be documented, so keep a paper trail from today. You'll have fifteen minutes. See you at four.

extra_audio.text: Fabiana manages the typhoon crisis. First, at seven, she sets up a war room with Marcus and triages the open orders. Then, at nine, she sends a status update to every stakeholder. Next, she calls Kevin Lin in Tainan and agrees on a workaround through Taichung. After that, at four, she presents the full picture to the leadership team. Finally, the following week, she leads a debrief and writes up the lessons.

items.situation: 7:05 a.m. Priya asks: what is the first thing you'll do?
tips: Triage. I'll check which orders are hit and which can wait a week.

items.situation: Greg asks if the Chicago order will be late.
tips: Two days at most. We're having the panels moved to Taichung, so we can get ahead of it.
have + object + past participle: someone else does it (Lesson 5).

items.situation: The CFO asks why this happened again.
tips: The supplier should have moved part of the order when the first warnings came out.
should have + past participle: what went wrong (Lesson 3).

items.situation: Priya asks for your recommendation in one sentence.
tips: We recommend that the Chicago order be shipped first and that the rest wait for Taichung.

items.situation: A board member asks if the second supplier was worth the money.
tips: Absolutely. If we hadn't added Monterrey, we would be out of stock today.
mixed conditional: past decision, present result (Lesson 8).

items.situation: Someone suggests skipping the debrief next week.
tips: I'd rather we didn't. It's time we learned from this, not just survived it.
